label: David Papineau, The Rise of Physicalism…: Causal influence: every occurrence of the target mental…
locator: pp.3–12 p.9 (Comments on the Causal Argument for Physicalism), premise 2 (causal influence)
interpretation: Papineau's premise 2, "All mental occurrences have physical effects", as a premise of the canonical causal argument. He treats its denial as epiphenomenalism or preestablished harmony (p.10), and allows a strict or a generous reading of causation for second-order states (p.11). Note 5 (in passage PAPINEAU-RISE-PHYSICALISM-13-33) makes the argument a schema for other special categories. The Lean predicate instantiates the premise at the frame's target kind. Papineau does not address the intellectual exercise of q.75; the application to it is not attributed to him.
